Control Accounts — Employees

Employee control accounts are special accounts in the general ledger that automatically consolidate all employee-related transactions into a single balance sheet account.

These accounts track amounts owed to or from employees, including salary advances, expense reimbursements, loans, and other employee-related financial transactions.

The system automatically maintains the balance of each control account by aggregating all individual employee balances from the subsidiary ledger.

Name
Name

The name identifies each employee control account in your chart of accounts.

Overview

Control accounts are summary accounts in the general ledger that represent the total of all individual employee balances in the subsidiary ledger.

An employee control account automatically consolidates all amounts owed to or from employees into a single balance sheet account, tracking employee-related financial transactions such as salary advances, expense reimbursements, or loan repayments.

Naming Guidelines

When naming employee control accounts, use descriptive names that clearly indicate the nature of employee transactions, such as Employee Advances, Staff Loans, Expense Claims Payable, or Employee Clearing Account.

Choose names that make it easy to identify the account's purpose when viewing financial reports or the chart of accounts.

Benefits and Best Practices

Benefits include simplified payroll and expense management, automatic tracking of employee-related assets and liabilities, and the ability to maintain detailed employee transaction records while keeping the general ledger organized.

Best practice: Create separate control accounts for different types of employee transactions (advances vs. expense claims) or employee groups (permanent staff vs. contractors) to facilitate better analysis and internal control.

Group
Group

The balance sheet group determines where this control account appears on your balance sheet.

Employee control accounts typically appear under Current Assets (for amounts owed by employees) or Current Liabilities (for amounts owed to employees), depending on the nature of the transactions.
